messages.content: 獲取蘋果公司、谷歌有限責任公司和微軟公司在紐約證券交易所的最新收盤價格和交易量。

function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to fetch latest close prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC (Alphabet?), Microsoft Corp on NYSE? Actually Apple trades on NASDAQ; but maybe they mean New York Stock Exchange? But we just need to call function with symbols.

Apple's ticker AAPL. Alphabet has GOOGL or GOOG. Microsoft MSFT. They all trade on Nasdaq though. We'll still provide data.

We should use function get_stock_data twice per symbol? Or one request each? We have only one function signature which takes symbol and data_points array. So we will make three calls:

1) symbol="AAPL", data_points=["price","volume"]
2) symbol="GOOGL", same
3) symbol="MSFT"

But note data_points expects either "price" or "volume". It says data_points: "price" | "volume"[] . That seems ambiguous: could pass an array containing strings "price" or "volume"? Probably yes. Provide ["price","volume"].

We'll produce separate responses after calling function thrice. Use tool invocation format. Let's do it sequentially.
